title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: November 2, 2026
headline: Gardner Minshew is the starting QB after Jacoby Brissett was demoted to third string; Michael Wilson is playing through two broken ribs, and Kendrick Bourne's injury looks bad.
summary: Coach Mike LaFleur confirmed that Gardner Minshew will start at quarterback, with Carson as the backup and Jacoby Brissett as the emergency third option. He called the change a collective decision that was meant to give the offense a spark, and said Minshew's play, including a seven-yard completion and accurate passing, changed the game's momentum. LaFleur said the run game's slow start came from execution problems he considers coaching issues. He praised Michael Wilson, who is playing through two broken ribs, and said Wilson's pain was managed rather than a risk of further injury. He gave no real update on Jeremiyah Love's new ankle issue, promising more Wednesday, and said Kendrick Bourne's news is not good and his season may be in doubt. Bam Knight and Jayden Williams are in concussion protocol with updates due Wednesday. LaFleur also discussed going onside in the fourth quarter, the team's 3-5 record, and the upcoming game against Seattle.

title: Joe Brady Evaluates Victory Over Baltimore Ravens And Development On Bills Defense
headline: Rousseau is playing outstanding edge football, Ed Oliver's return is helping the pass rush, and Damar Hamlin was 'as consistent as can be' while the starting safety spot stays open until C.J. Gardner-Johnson's return is evaluated.
summary: Coach Joe Brady said the medical staff's injury evaluations come after the team meetings, and he would have more personnel answers by Wednesday. He praised Gregory Rousseau's development, crediting his mindset and the outside linebacker room with Bradley Chubb and TJ Parker, and said Rousseau is impacting the quarterback even without many sacks. He was pleased with Ed Oliver's return, saying it helps the whole rotation. On penalties, Brady said he wants the team in the middle of the league rather than the cleanest, and he has no patience for pre-snap penalties, which included offensive holds, illegal formations, and two offside calls. He defended taking the ball after winning the toss, saying the team wants to start fast and that Josh Allen needed to be on the field from the start. He also explained the late-half clock decision: taking time off the clock made the defense more predictable for a short field-goal attempt. On the safety position, Brady said Damar Hamlin was as consistent as can be and that several backups stepped up, but the decision on the starter will wait for a coordinator review. He said there has been no communication with C.J. Gardner-Johnson for about a week, and Gardner-Johnson was in meetings that day.

Jaelan Phillips is trending in the right direction and is viewed as day-to-day, but the coach wants him to handle a full workload, not just a few high-speed efforts. Will Lee is also day-to-day, in rehab, with tests planned later this week. On the defense, Canales praised Marco Wilson's aggressive play, including the penalty he took, and said Wilson will be on the field. He also said the Broncos' balanced offense and consistent defense make them a difficult matchup. The D'Angelo Hall hire was described as a way to add a coach for the cornerbacks while keeping Ronald Curry-style secondary coverage intact, and Canales said the decision was driven by his personal regard for Hall. He noted the team's takeaways have not converted into enough points, a problem he is addressing with the offensive staff.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference: November 2nd, 2026
headline: No new injuries out of the Pittsburgh loss, Harold Fannin Jr.'s target share is rising, and Todd Monken blamed the eight sacks on the whole offense rather than Deshaun Watson alone.
summary: Monken said the eight sacks came from a mix of factors: pass protection, quick releases, and Watson's own decisions. He pointed mainly to falling behind early, which pushed the offense into obvious passing situations and left it unable to stay ahead of the chains. He said the running game stalled because the team never found a rhythm and lost explosive and auxiliary runs once it trailed. He admitted the offensive line was not where he wanted it and said the team would keep working on scheme and execution. On defense, he said the Steelers' attack-style runs and trap plays beat them with explosives and missed tackles, and that the defense has to fit gaps and tackle better. He called Harold Fannin Jr. an improving receiver and said the team wants to spread targets across its young skill players, with Denzel Boston's connections still lagging. He said Carson Schwesinger's ankle has not shown up on film and that no one else came out of the game with a new injury.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Saleh: no injury update until Wednesday after the bye; JFM is playing through a serious back injury at about 75%
summary: Saleh opened by saying the team is still evaluating some injuries and won't have an update until Wednesday of next week, after the bye. He credited Cam Ward with finally getting the numbers he'd been working toward, citing teammates' plays, yards after catch, Tony Pollard's running, and play-action designs. He said the offense is still young and left yards on the field, with ball security and a late-game timing issue still needing cleanup. On penalties, he said the team ranks near the top of the league in fewest, and he called post-snap and pre-snap penalties the ones to eliminate while accepting some flags as the cost of an aggressive style. He said the veteran receivers have been dropping too many critical passes and that contested catches need work. On defense, he praised Amani Hooker's pre-snap diagnosis and Jacob Martin's effort, and he said the young group, including Gunnar Helm and the rookies, is still growing. He said John Franklin-Myers is battling a serious back injury and is still suiting up, and he said the first eight weeks have been adversity-heavy but the locker room is buying in.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 11/02/26
headline: Antonio Williams' role keeps growing with Terry McLaurin out, and Dan Quinn praised Charles Omenihu and Dorance Armstrong Jr. up front, while Daron Payne's absence is a concern.
summary: Quinn said the team needed time to reset after the bye and was pleased with the resilience shown in a division win over Philadelphia, even after falling behind 10-0. He credited the defense for improving on third down and the defensive line for rushing better together, and said the offense put together good drives after a slow start. Special teams provided a spark, including Luke McCaffrey's return work and a late punt return. Penalties remain his main frustration, with seven in the first half, and he said the pre-snap issues, especially on the inside, still need investigation and correction. He said Jayden Daniels showed poise and ball security, and that the receivers are cleaner in route running with better rotation of locations. Antonio Williams drew high praise for handling a bigger role without Terry McLaurin, and Quinn said Burks made a big impact with a double move. Daron Payne's injury, which Quinn said was not a freak play, was a significant blow, but the line still produced four sacks, with Omenihu and Armstrong standing out inside.
